countries/Austria: "is constitutionally neutral and stays outside military alliances" - neutral by constitutional law and not in NATO, but EU membership carries a mutual-assistance clause; a reader may see that as alliance-like
countries/Denmark: "shares its only mainland border with a larger southern neighbour" - worded 'mainland' because since 2022 the realm also has a short land border on a small Arctic island with a North American state
countries/Germany: "has a capital that was once split between rival states" - the eastern half was the eastern state's capital, while the western half was not formally the western state's capital
"has the largest economy of any state in Europe" - true by nominal GDP for decades; a ranking that could in principle change
countries/Iceland: "was uninhabited until seafaring settlers arrived in the Middle Ages" - a few hermit monks may have been present shortly before the main ninth-century settlement; both fall in the Middle Ages
countries/Iraq: "has long been among the world's leading growers of date palms" - historically the top producer; its current rank among producers is lower and varies year to year
countries/Jamaica: "has long been a major producer of bauxite and alumina" - historically among the largest producers; its current world rank is lower (roughly top ten)
countries/Norway: "was ruled for centuries by neighbouring kingdoms before full independence" - centuries in union under a southern neighbour's crown, then 1814-1905 in a union with its own parliament; 'ruled' is a simplification for the last period
countries/Poland: "has a northeastern lake district with thousands of lakes" - the usual figure is about two thousand lakes
